newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico family, Belgian student killed in crash.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico family, Belgian student killed in crash.

text.p: Three members of a New Mexico family and a Belgian exchange student were killed on Friday when their sports utility vehicle crashed into a tractor trailer and both vehicles went up in flames, police said.

Officer Florian Chavez of the New Mexico State Police said the accident occured on Interstate highway 40, about 80 miles (130 km) west of Albuquerque, when the sports utility vehicle swerved out of the westbound lane, crossed the median and ploughed head on into an eastbound tractor trailer rig.
"It looks like they died on impact," said Chavez. "The driver of the rig got out before it burned."

Police Capt. Rudy Acosta identified the dead driver of the sports utility vehicle as Faith Bannister, 44, whose husband Mark Bannister, a district attorney from Tucumcari, New Mexico, commited suicide last year. Acosta said two of Bannister's teenage children and a Belgian exchange student who has not been identified also died in the crash.
Police said the Bannisters are survived by their 12-year-old son, who was at the family home in Tucumcari at the time of the crash.
